blogTitle: What are the Best Paint Colors for Small Rooms?
videoTitle: What are the Best Paint Colors for Small Rooms?
script:
What are the Best Paint Colors for Small Rooms?

[warmly] You know that feeling when you walk into a small room and the walls just… close in on you? The right paint colour can completely change that.

Here's the thing — light paint colours REFLECT more natural and artificial light around the space, which reduces shadows and makes walls appear to recede.

I had a client with a dark navy kitchen — honestly, she felt boxed in every single day… we switched to a soft cream with pale green undertones and she said the room just BREATHES.

Light colours blur edges, hide tight corners, and trick the eye into thinking the space is LARGER — it really is that simple.

Now, neutrals… they are honestly one of my favourites for compact spaces — think soft cream, warm taupe, light grey, muted beige — calm and TIMELESS.

A little tip I love: avoid muddy or dark neutral tones — instead, choose ones with a SUBTLE hint of warmth or coolness to keep the room bright and cosy at the same time.

[excited] And then there are cool tones — pale blues, soft greens, gentle lilacs — they create this sense of DISTANCE, like the walls are just… drifting away from you.

Cool tones work BEST when they're paired with natural light and simple calm decor — keep it uncluttered and let the colour do the work, you know?

Here's something people often overlook — the FINISH matters just as much as the colour… eggshell or satin finishes bounce light around the room beautifully.

Trust me — keep your trim and ceiling in the SAME pale family as your walls and the whole room just… opens up, without touching a single wall.

Now — wall art and paint colour… this is where it gets really fun… the paint is your CANVAS and the art should feel like it belongs there, not fight the wall.

A simple rule I always share: match at least ONE tone in your wall art to your paint colour — it creates this effortless, COHESIVE feel that just looks considered.

[warmly] These are perfect for a hallway with those cool tones we talked about — a set of two Boho Women prints that feel calm and artful without overwhelming a narrow space.

For a compact bedroom — soft cream or warm taupe walls… and art that feels personal and serene… like this set of three Boho Women prints in warm earthy tones.

And if your small room has cool blue or sage tones on the walls, these three Botanical prints are MADE for that palette — soft, natural, and perfectly tonal.

For a tiny living room, a calm neutral wall really lets statement art sing — like these two Asian-inspired prints… understated, but they make the room feel CONSIDERED.

These Italian lifestyle prints work beautifully against a light grey with blue undertones — that cool-neutral wall makes the warm tones in the art just POP without clashing.

Room by room — narrow hallway? Go cool and LIGHT. Compact bedroom? Warm neutrals. Tiny living room? Pale blues or creams… each room has its sweet spot.

[sighs] And the colours to AVOID… dark saturated shades, very stark clinical whites, muddy heavy tones — they shrink the room and just drain the energy right out of it.

So the key takeaways — light soft shades, eggshell or satin finish, keep trim and ceiling in the same pale family… and choose wall art that ECHOES your palette… and your small room won't feel small at all.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
